item.title: NASA Eyes Crop Candidates for Future Menus
item.description: As NASA prepares for future missions to the Moon and Mars, researchers are studying crops that could provide astronauts with fresh food, nutrition, and variety far from Earth. Such crop variety can help with menus in deep space, something top of mind this week as the nation celebrates Thanksgiving.

item.title: Childhood, Career Come Full Circle for Budget Analyst at NASA Goddard
item.description: Conversations about NASA were the norm around the dinner table during Ashley Knight’s childhood. Her parents worked at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, and discussions about happenings at the agency continued even when they came home from the office.

item.title: Eye of the Sahara
item.description: The Richat Structure, also known as the “Eye of the Sahara,” is seen from the International Space Station as it orbited above on Nov. 14, 2026.

item.title: NASA’s Hubble Views Ocean of Stars in Groundwork for Roman
item.description: These Hubble observations are part of a survey that will help researchers better interpret upcoming Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope observations as they seek to characterize the stars and search for exoplanets in this busy region of our galaxy.

item.title: Learnings and Pitfalls from AI-Assisted A/B Experimentation at Scale
item.description: A/B testing underpins product decisions by providing trustworthy, reproducible quantification of proposed changes' effects. Growing large language model (LLM) capabilities have motivated efforts to automate experimentation workflows.

item.title: Where Did My Tokens Go? Verifiable Token Billing for LLM Services
item.description: Users of large language model (LLM) services receive token bills with limited evidence of which calls incurred their charges. In broker-mediated agent workflows, calls arise after authorization and billing evidence spans service domains.

item.title: ExpGuard: Guarding Long-Horizon LLM Agents against Corrupted Experience
item.description: Long-horizon large language model (LLM) agents distill past trajectories into reusable experiences. Misleading or adversarial guidance in source trajectories can corrupt these experiences, allowing harmful instructions to persist across tasks and influence future agent actions.

item.title: SkillBoost: A Constrained Exploration-Exploitation Process for Mitigating Skill Overfitting
item.description: Enabling large language model (LLM) agents to accumulate and reuse experience from past interactions remains a central challenge in real-world applications. A promising solution is to treat skills as trainable states and optimize them in the same way as model parameters in neural network training.

item.title: RESET: One Demonstration, One Verified World, Self-Improved Skills Across Embodiments
item.description: Large language model (LLM) coding agents can iteratively self-improve robot manipulation skills in simulation benchmarks, yet real-world tasks provide neither ground-truth success scorers nor resettable practice environments. item.title: ActiveBridge: Scaling Active Prior for Robots through Egocentric Perception-Interaction Modeling
item.description: Robotics foundation models are now widely used for manipulation, and egocentric videos offer rich data for scaling. However, existing methods overlook the human active priors captured in egocentric videos, which limits performance in unstructured scenes.

item.title: EgoLoAF: Learning Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from Egocentric Demonstrations with Hand-Object Affordances
item.description: Training humanoid vision-language-action (VLA) models relies heavily on costly real-robot teleoperation. Recent efforts convert egocentric human demonstrations into humanoid training data.

item.title: Joint Classification and Generation on Tabular Data: an Empirical Study
item.description: Many applications of machine learning on tabular data need both a classifier and a generator of realistic records. The default is to train two separate models, whereas a single joint model promises both from one set of weights.

item.title: Hardware-tailored logical Clifford circuits for stabilizer codes
item.description: Quantum error correction is the art of protecting fragile quantum information through suitable encoding and active interventions. However, it is notoriously difficult to manipulate encoded quantum data without causing uncorrectable errors.

item.title: Real-time adaptive quantum error correction by multi-agent learning
item.description: Quantum error correction is essential for scalable quantum computing, yet existing approaches rely on static assumptions about noise that break down in realistic hardware where error channels drift over time. item.title: Detailed, interpretable characterization of mid-circuit measurement on a transmon qubit
item.description: Mid-circuit measurements (MCMs) are critical components of the quantum error correction protocols expected to enable utility-scale quantum computing. MCMs can be modeled by quantum instruments (a type of quantum operation or process), which can be characterized self-consistently using gate set tomography.
